title: Print a shared node once

tests.expr: (dbl := lambda n, e: e if n == 0 else (lambda d: Add(d, d))(dbl(n - 1, e)), emit(dbl(3, Var('x'))))[-1]
tests.expect: int32_t v0 = (int32_t)((uint32_t)x + (uint32_t)x); | int32_t v1 = (int32_t)((uint32_t)v0 + (uint32_t)v0); | int32_t v2 = (int32_t)((uint32_t)v1 + (uint32_t)v1); => v2

tests.expr: (s := Add(Var('a'), Lit(1)), emit(Add(Mul(s, Lit(2)), Mul(s, Lit(3)))))[-1]
tests.expect: int32_t v0 = (int32_t)((uint32_t)a + (uint32_t)1); | int32_t v1 = (int32_t)((uint32_t)v0 * (uint32_t)2); | int32_t v2 = (int32_t)((uint32_t)v0 * (uint32_t)3); | int32_t v3 = (int32_t)((uint32_t)v1 + (uint32_t)v2); => v3
int32_t v0 = (int32_t)((uint32_t)a + (uint32_t)1); | int32_t v1 = (int32_t)((uint32_t)a + (uint32_t)1); | int32_t v2 = (int32_t)((uint32_t)v0 * (uint32_t)v1); => v2

tests.expr: (dbl := lambda n, e: e if n == 0 else (lambda d: Add(d, d))(dbl(n - 1, e)), r := emit(dbl(12, Var('x'))), ([str(len(r[0]))], r[1]))[-1]

hints: The table `names` is there and nothing uses it yet. It should map a node you have already printed to the C name you gave it.
Use `id(e)` as the key. `id` is different for every object, so two nodes that were built separately stay separate even when they look equal.
Before the two `go` calls: `if id(e) in names: return names[id(e)]`. After `lines.append(...)`: `names[id(e)] = v`.
explain: The reference looks the node up in `names` before it walks into the sources, and returns the saved name when it is there. After printing a line it saves the new name under `id(e)`. A node used twice is now printed once, and because the lookup comes first, its sources are not walked a second time either.
